key_herbs: Trikatu: Shunthi (Zingiber officinale), Maricha (Piper nigrum), Pippali (Piper longum)
Triphala: Haritaki (Terminalia chebula), Bibhitaki (Terminalia bellirica), Amalaki (Phyllanthus emblica)
description_en: A sugar-containing purgative powder of Trikatu, Triphala and turpeth, used for pitta disorders.
anupana: Lukewarm water on an empty stomach
safety_note: Purgative: avoid in pregnancy, diarrhoea or dehydration; sugar content matters for diabetics; Embelia and turpeth are not well studied for safety.
evidence_note: No good clinical trials of this specific formulation; support is traditional use and laboratory data.

description_en: An astringent 26-herb powder traditionally used for abnormal vaginal discharge and bleeding disorders.
safety_note: Licorice component can raise blood pressure/lower potassium with heavy use; avoid in pregnancy unless supervised; persistent abnormal bleeding needs medical diagnosis.
evidence_note: No good clinical trials of this specific formulation; support is traditional use and laboratory data.

key_herbs: Rasna (Pluchea lanceolata, per general Ayurvedic sources; not verified on fetched pages)
description_en: A bitter-pungent decoction used for vata-type joint and nerve disorders.
safety_note: Guduchi has been linked to herb-induced liver injury; avoid in autoimmune disease and pregnancy unless supervised.
evidence_note: No good clinical trials of this specific formulation; support is traditional use and laboratory data.

description_en: A guduchi-based decoction traditionally used for gout and skin disorders.
safety_note: Guduchi has been linked to liver injury in India; avoid with autoimmune disease or liver disease.
evidence_note: No good clinical trials of this specific formulation; support is traditional use and laboratory data.

description_en: A bitter decoction led by neem, used traditionally for skin disease and abscesses.
safety_note: Neem may lower blood sugar and is traditionally avoided in pregnancy; neem oil is toxic to small children; guduchi has liver-injury reports.
evidence_note: Neem has insufficient clinical evidence; this decoction is untested.

key_herbs: Varuna (Crateva nurvala; general Ayurvedic sources, not verified on fetched pages)
description_en: A 15-herb decoction used for kapha-type disorders such as obesity and urinary complaints.
evidence_note: No good clinical trials of this specific formulation; support is traditional use and laboratory data.

description_en: Fruit powder of puncture vine used traditionally for urinary and prostate complaints.
anupana: Lukewarm water, tender coconut water or Brihatyadi kashayam
safety_note: NCCIH-cited note: not proven safe; rare liver toxicity suggested; avoid in pregnancy; hormonal claims unproven.
evidence_note: Controlled studies show no consistent testosterone effect; no strong human trials for urinary uses.

description_en: Stem powder of heart-leaved moonseed, a classic rasayana for immunity and metabolic complaints.
safety_note: Supplement use has been linked to herb-induced liver injury in India, sometimes severe; avoid in autoimmune disease, liver disease and pregnancy; may lower blood sugar.
evidence_note: Reviews find no good clinical evidence of benefit.

description_en: Bark powder of the arjuna tree, a classical heart tonic.
safety_note: Safety is not well documented; use cautiously with cardiac medicines and seek medical care for heart disease.
evidence_note: Wikipedia lists only preclinical studies; clinical evidence is limited.

indications_modern: Burning sensation in hands and feet
description_en: Root powder of Shatavari, traditionally a women's tonic and cooling rasayana.
safety_note: Safety not well studied; avoid in pregnancy unless supervised; may affect blood sugar.
evidence_note: Preliminary trials only; Wikipedia notes high-quality evidence is lacking.

description_en: Rhizome powder of sweet flag, used traditionally for mental clarity and digestive gas.
safety_note: Contains beta-asarone, considered carcinogenic in animals; US FDA banned calamus in food in 1968; can cause vomiting; Ayurvedic purification lowers beta-asarone; avoid in pregnancy.
evidence_note: No clinical evidence of safety or efficacy.

description_en: Powdered licorice root used for throat, eye and mouth complaints.
safety_note: Glycyrrhizin can cause high blood pressure, low potassium and arrhythmia with long or heavy use; avoid in pregnancy, hypertension, heart or kidney disease; interacts with corticosteroids.
evidence_note: Weak, preliminary evidence (e.g. mouth rinses, sore throat); not enough to support any condition.

description_en: Root powder of Indian snakeroot, source of reserpine, used for hypertension and sleeplessness.
safety_note: Contains reserpine-type alkaloids; can cause depression, nasal congestion, dizziness, GI upset; interacts with antihypertensives and antidepressants; avoid in depression, ulcer and pregnancy.
evidence_note: Reserpine lowered systolic BP about 8 mmHg in a review; whole-root powder lacks trials.

description_en: Root powder of hogweed, a classic diuretic and anti-swelling herb.
safety_note: Safety not documented in sources found; diuretic effect may interact with diuretics and affect kidney function.
evidence_note: Only lab studies such as lunamarine in vitro; no human trials found.

description_en: Tuber powder of nut grass, used for poor digestion and loose stools.
evidence_note: Little clinical evidence; traditional and laboratory data only.

description_en: Long pepper fruit powder, used for cough and sluggish digestion.
safety_note: May cause heartburn; large amounts avoided in pregnancy and with stomach ulcers; may alter drug absorption (piperine, general knowledge).
evidence_note: No clinical trials for these uses on the pages reviewed.

description_en: Garlic-based tablet containing purified sulphur, used for colicky gut disorders.
safety_note: Garlic may raise bleeding risk with anticoagulants and interact with some drugs; stop before surgery; contains processed sulphur.
evidence_note: Garlic evidence is mixed; no trials of this tablet.

description_en: A multi-herb digestive tablet; some versions include purified aconite and mineral components.
safety_note: Formulations vary; some contain processed aconite (Vatsanabha), which is toxic if mis-processed; calamus contains beta-asarone; avoid in pregnancy.
evidence_note: Traditional use; no robust human trials.

description_en: A small aromatic Kerala tablet used for cough, hiccup, vomiting and breathlessness.
safety_note: Contains camphor; avoid in infants and in pregnancy unless supervised.
evidence_note: No trials found; traditional use only.

description_en: A proprietary tablet of Embelia, hibiscus and asafoetida for menstrual pain.
safety_note: Embelia has been used as a contraceptive/abortifacient in some traditions; avoid in pregnancy; proprietary, not classical.
evidence_note: Proprietary product, no trials found; weakly sourced.

description_en: A turmeric, ghee and sugar confection with iron ash, used for allergic skin conditions.
safety_note: Sugar content matters for diabetics; contains Loha bhasma (iron); turmeric supplements can rarely cause liver injury; avoid in pregnancy unless supervised.
evidence_note: Turmeric evidence is weak; no trials of this formula.

description_en: A jaggery-based confection of kantakari and spices used for cough and hiccup.
safety_note: Sugar/jaggery content; Solanum fruit is poisonous in raw form; guduchi liver-injury reports; plumbago (Chitraka) is irritant and avoided in pregnancy.
evidence_note: Lab-level studies of Solanum only; no trials of this formula.

description_en: A fermented iron-containing tonic traditionally used for anaemia.
safety_note: Self-generated alcohol; contains processed iron (avoid with haemochromatosis, caution with iron supplements); heavy-metal contamination risk in some Ayurvedic products; avoid in pregnancy and with diabetes unless supervised.
evidence_note: No trials found; NCCIH notes evidence for Ayurveda is limited and metal safety is a concern.

description_en: A raisin and honey confection used as a tonic for anaemia and weakness.
safety_note: Sugar and honey content matters for diabetics; licorice component warrants caution with hypertension.
evidence_note: No trials found.

key_herbs: Dashamoola (ten roots; includes Aegle marmelos, Solanum virginianum, Tribulus terrestris)
description_en: A coarse powder of ten roots decocted for vata disorders, joint pain and respiratory complaints.
safety_note: Pregnancy caution; decoction preparation varies.
evidence_note: Ten roots in classical combination; no strong clinical data found.

description_en: A medicated sesame oil applied to the head for eye, ear and sinus complaints.
safety_note: External use only; may cause cold or sinus congestion if applied wet or over long periods; caution with sensitive skin; contains galena (lead sulphide) per parsed record, a heavy-metal concern.
evidence_note: Traditional use only.
